before.text:
Abstract

                                                         We establish a new decoupling inequality for curves in the spirit of [B-D1],[B-D2] which implies a new mean
                                                   value theorem for certain exponential sums crucial to the Bombieri-Iwaniec method as developed further in [H].
                                                   In particular, this leads to an improved bound |ζ( 12 + it)| ≪ t13/84+ε for the zeta function on the critical line.

unit_result_entry.title: Holder reduction to a sixfold first-spacing distribution
unit_result_entry.why_material: An interval-count estimate, the preliminary sum bound, and sixth-power Holder produce a dichotomy: either a direct bound holds or the problem reduces to a bilinear sum coupling interval phase vectors with a sixfold convolution of the first-spacing curve.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Includes the admissible Q range and the definition of the six-coordinate aggregate y(h).
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (3.5)-(3.7) and the displayed y(h) vector.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Reduction of smooth exponential sums to interval phase vectors
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The application fixes derivative nondegeneracy, introduces the intermediate scales N and R, and cites the established Bombieri-Iwaniec reduction that bounds the original sum using short sums indexed by minor-arc intervals and four-dimensional phase vectors.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Double large sieve separates the two spacing problems
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The double large sieve bounds the coupled phase sum by the geometric mean of a first-spacing count A and a second-spacing count B1, times coordinate-volume factors, cleanly isolating what the new mean-value theorem can control from what must be imported.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The sharp A6 estimate controls exactly the first-spacing count A in the double large sieve; when paired with separately sourced second-spacing bounds and optimized intermediate scales, it improves smooth exponential sums, and complementary range estimates plus the approximate functional equation transfer that improvement to the critical line.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source does not derive the second-spacing estimates, the complementary Huxley/exponent-pair bounds, or the approximate functional equation; the final implication is therefore a composite result rather than decoupling alone.
